title: Clarence Potter and his Jazz Babies, a flop in Hoboken
summary: His first New York contact was singer Clarence Potter, who imitated Harry Lauder; their act was so bad the Hoboken manager just paid carfare.

bands.name: Clarence Potter and his Jazz Babies

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That's beautiful. I totally agree with you. What took place after you got to New York -- with your music?
Well, my first recollection of contact

with musicians was a fellow by the name of Clarence Potter. He heard about this clarinet player from Ohio -- it was a big joke -- This Clarence Potter was a very dark Negro who had sharp, sharp features and he did Scottish imitations. He imitated Sir Harry Lauder. He sang in Scotch, he did the number, he wore kilts, and did everything like Harry Lauder. Clarence Potter.

A singer, singer, yeah. He sang songs just like Harry Lauder sings, in Scotch, and he was real dark but he had real sharp features. Looked as though -- like some other race, blacked up -- that's the way he looked. Very handsome guy, short and stocky. So we rehearsed for about three or four weeks and had this act. He had been an entertainer around New York, you know. In those days entertaining, singing musicians were the thing. You know, if you couldn't sing, you didn't make the money. It wasn't so much dance as it was entertainment. And we had an act formed -- Clarence Potter and his Jazz Babies.

Yes. So, we had a Sunday concert -- they called them concerts because at the burlesque houses they didn't work burlesque on Sunday, so they had vaudeville on Sundays. So we did this Sunday concert at the Lyric's Lyric in Hoboken, New Jersey -- last town in the world -- Hoboken. Well, let me tell you, the act was so bad, after the first show the manager came
back and gave us two dollars and a half for our transportation back to Manhattan.
Well, we had a five-piece band and a singer.
